key_insight: LLMs can estimate PTSD severity from natural-language narratives, but their accuracy depends strongly on available contextual knowledge and the modeling/prompting strategies used; providing the right context and design choices meaningfully improves performance.
problem_solved: Clarifies which factors (contextual information and modeling choices) influence the reliability of zero-shot LLM-based PTSD severity estimation, addressing uncertainty about when and how to trust these models in clinical-text settings.
method: Compiled a clinical dataset of 1,437 natural-language trauma narratives paired with self-reported PTSD severity scores.
Evaluated 11 state-of-the-art LLMs in a zero-shot setting and compared outputs against ground-truth severity.
Systematically varied contextual knowledge (e.g., available clinical/demographic cues) and modeling strategies (prompt templates, response scoring/mapping) to quantify effects on accuracy.
impact: Provides actionable evidence for AI/ML practitioners to prioritize contextual features and careful prompt/scoring design when adapting LLMs for mental health assessment, and highlights limits of off-the-shelf zero-shot use in clinical contexts.
visual_elements: Bar chart: model performance (accuracy/MAE/AUC) for each LLM with and without added context
Flow diagram: experimental pipeline — dataset → model variants → prompt/strategy variants → evaluation metrics
Heatmap or violin plot: effect sizes of different contextual cues and modeling strategies on prediction error
Annotated example: sample narrative with predicted vs. true PTSD severity to illustrate common success/failure modes
paper_title: A Systematic Evaluation of Large Language Models for PTSD Severity Estimation: The Role of Contextual Knowledge and Modeling Strategies
paper_authors: Panagiotis Kaliosis, Adithya V Ganesan, Oscar N. E. Kjell, Whitney Ringwald, Scott Feltman
